answer: Requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn turns identity into a cost: one operator can spawn an ocean of fake accounts, but each must post its own collateral, so a Sybil flood drains the attacker instead of the reward pool. Misbehavior slashes the stake and whispers the penalty through shared reputation, so a burned identity cannot regrow like a willow cut back — it must pay again to return.
